2
Which quantity is not an SI base quantity?
A
charge
B
mass
C
temperature
D
time

hints: Notice the question asks for the quantity that is not an SI base quantity, so recall the seven-member base list and see which of charge, mass, temperature and time is missing.
Remember that in electricity the SI base quantity is electric current in ampere $\text{A}$, while charge in coulomb $\text{C}$ is formed from other quantities.
Check mass in $\text{kg}$, temperature in $\text{K}$ and time in $\text{s}$ against the base list, then use $Q = It$ to show charge is derived.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: four quantities - charge, mass, temperature and time - and the task is to find the one that is not an SI base quantity.
Recall the SI base quantities include mass, thermodynamic temperature, time, electric current, length, amount of substance and luminous intensity.
Note that charge is not on that list because it is defined from base quantities by $Q = It$, giving the derived unit $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.
Check the other three: mass has base unit kilogram $\text{kg}$, thermodynamic temperature has base unit kelvin $\text{K}$, and time has base unit second $\text{s}$.
Therefore charge is the only derived quantity in the list. This is option A.

A.explanation: Charge is a derived quantity with unit coulomb, defined by $Q = It$ as $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.

B.explanation: Mass is an SI base quantity with base unit kilogram $\text{kg}$.

C.explanation: Thermodynamic temperature is an SI base quantity with base unit kelvin $\text{K}$.

D.explanation: Time is an SI base quantity with base unit second $\text{s}$.
